The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

content:
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

content:
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

content:
# Tabs

Use Tabs to switch between a few related views of the same subject, one view visible at a time.

A row of labeled tabs above a single panel. Choosing a tab shows its panel in place and hides the others, without leaving the page. One tab is always selected.

## When to use

- Split a settings page into a few peer sections, such as Profile, Notifications, and Billing.
- Show different views of the same item, such as an order's Details, Shipments, and History.

## When not to use

- Move between separate pages, where each choice changes the address. Use [Link](component.link) instead. Navigation between pages belongs to links, so the address, history, and back button work.
- Choose a value that is saved or submitted with a form. Use [Radio group](component.radio-group) instead. Tabs change what is shown, not what is stored. A radio group records the choice.
- Walk through steps that must be completed in order. Instead: A step-by-step flow with previous and next actions. Tabs imply the sections are peers that can be visited in any order.
- Content people need to compare side by side or read straight through. Instead: Headings in one scrolling page. Tabs hide every panel but one, so comparison means switching back and forth.
- Show or hide one section on its own, independent of the others. Use [Accordion](component.accordion) instead. Tabs always show exactly one panel. Independent sections need their own toggle.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| section | container | One tab and the content of its panel. The sections are peers in a set. |
| tab-list | container | The row of tabs, labeled as a set. |
| tab | interactive-surface | One labeled tab that selects its panel. |
| selected-indicator | indicator | Bar along the bottom edge of the selected tab, the full width of the tab, that shows which panel is visible. |
| panel | container | The content of the selected section, shown below the tab list. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| accessibleName | string |  |  | Accessible name for the set of tabs. It is not shown; a visible heading above the tabs usually says the same thing. |
| value | string |  |  | The value of the selected section. Empty or unmatched selects the first section. |

## Events

- `change`: The selected tab changed from user interaction.

## Items

### section

Options of each `section`.

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string |  |  | Visible text of the section's tab, and its accessible name. Required. |
| value | string |  |  | Identifies the section. Unique within the set; the value parameter selects the section whose value it matches. |

## States

`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `selected`

## Rules

Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **MUST** labels-short-and-unique: Each tab has a short label that differs from the others. The set has an accessible name.
  - Do: Profile, Notifications, Billing
  - Avoid: Profile settings, Notification settings, Billing settings
- **MUST** unique-values: Each section has a value that differs from the others, so the value parameter selects exactly one section.
  - See: component.tabs#items.section.parameters.value
- **SHOULD** few-tabs: Keep to a handful of tabs that fit in one row at common widths. A row that overflows scrolls sideways, and tabs off screen are easy to miss.

### Behavior

- **MUST** one-selected: Exactly one tab is selected, and only its panel is shown or exposed to assistive technology. When the value matches no section, the first section is selected.
- **MUST** selection-reports-change: Selecting a different tab by pointer or keyboard reports change. Setting the value programmatically, or choosing the tab that is already selected, reports nothing.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** keyboard-tabs: Tab enters the tab list at the selected tab and leaves it for the panel. The arrow keys along the row move focus and selection to the next or previous tab in reading direction, wrapping at either end. Home and End move to the first and last tab.
- **MUST** panel-reachable: The panel is the next keyboard stop after the tab list, so its content can be reached and read even when it holds nothing focusable.
- **MUST** accessible-tabs: The tab list is named by the accessibleName parameter. Each tab exposes its label and whether it is selected, and the panel is named by the selected tab.
- **MUST** forced-colors: The selected tab is marked by an indicator, not by color alone, and the indicator and keyboard focus stay visible under forced colors.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.

## Accessibility

- Role: A tab list of tabs, and one tab panel for the selected tab.
- Name: The tab list from the accessibleName parameter. Each tab from its section's label. The panel from the selected tab.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Enter the tab list at the selected tab, then move to the panel. |
| Arrow keys | Move focus and selection to the next or previous tab in reading direction, with wrapping. |
| Home | Move focus and selection to the first tab. |
| End | Move focus and selection to the last tab. |

## Rationale

- **Arrowing to a tab selects it and shows its panel.** Panels are already on the page, so showing one costs nothing, and selection that follows focus saves a keystroke. Manual activation suits panels that load slowly, which Tabs does not support. There is no parameter for it.
- **Tabs sit in one horizontal row. There is no vertical orientation.** A row above the panel is the common case. A vertical list beside the panel is closer to navigation and can be added as a parameter when a product needs it. There is one size, set by the label typography.
- **Sections are items, and each section owns its label and value.** Each section carries a label, a value, and rich content, so they are options of the section, not of the whole set (ADR 0004). Accordion's sections are items the same way. The order of the sections is the order of the tabs.
- **Tabs have no disabled state.** A disabled tab shows a section that cannot be opened and hides why. Leave out a section that does not apply, or show it and explain inside its panel what is needed.
- **Selection is a state, and it never syncs with the address.** Selected is the one persistent state. When a choice should change the address, it is navigation and belongs to links (see the avoid entries). A product can still read and set the value itself.
- **Tabs have no loading or invalid state.** Tabs show content the page already has and store nothing, so there is nothing to wait on or validate. A panel that loads its own content shows its own progress.
- **One density. A long row scrolls sideways.** Tab padding keeps a comfortable target. Too many tabs to fit is a content problem (few-tabs), so scrolling is the fallback, not a compact mode.
- **Every tab has a text label.** Tab labels come from the section's label, which is text. An icon without words would need a separate accessible name and is hard to scan in a row.
- **Tab order and arrow keys follow the reading direction.** In a right-to-left layout the first tab sits at the right and the left arrow moves to the next tab. Nothing is mirrored artwork.
- **Selection changes instantly. Nothing animates.** An instant change needs no reduced motion treatment, and a sliding indicator would delay reading the new panel.
- **The selected indicator is a bar on the bottom edge of the selected tab, as wide as the tab, and as thick as the semantic indicator width.** A bar under the label points at the panel below it. It sits on the tab list's divider line, inside the row, so a row that scrolls sideways does not clip it. Its thickness is a token, so it changes with the system's other selection bars rather than being fixed in each implementation.
- **Forced colors keep the indicator and focus through system colors.** The indicator takes the system highlight and focus rings keep their outline, so selection and focus never depend on the theme colors (forced-colors).
- **Tabs consume semantic colors and typography, with spacing primitives.** Tokens ADR 0003. The selected indicator borrows the primary action fill as the strongest accent the system has, and hover borrows the tertiary action hover because a tab is a low-emphasis control. No semantic spacing role exists, so spacing primitives set padding and gaps.

## Links

### alternative

- [Accordion](component.accordion) — Show or hide one section on its own, independent of the others. Tabs always show exactly one panel. Independent sections need their own toggle.
- [Link](component.link) — Move between separate pages, where each choice changes the address. Navigation between pages belongs to links, so the address, history, and back button work.
- [Radio group](component.radio-group) — Choose a value that is saved or submitted with a form. Tabs change what is shown, not what is stored. A radio group records the choice.

### alternative-to

- [Accordion](component.accordion) — Switch between a few peer views of the same subject, one visible at a time. Tabs keep the choices in one row and always show one view. An accordion stacks headings and can show several sections or none.
- [Card](component.card) — Switch between related views of the same subject. Tabs show one view at a time in place. Cards show several subjects side by side.
- [Link](component.link) — Switch between a few views of the same subject without leaving the page. Tabs show one view in place. A link changes the address.
- [Radio group](component.radio-group) — Switch which view of the same subject is shown, without saving a choice. Tabs change what is shown. A radio group records a value.

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

### related

- [Link](component.link)
- [Radio group](component.radio-group)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-tabs>`

### Import

```js
import { defineTabs } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/tabs";

defineTabs();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-tabs label="Account settings" value="profile">
  <ds-tab-panel label="Profile" value="profile">…</ds-tab-panel>
  <ds-tab-panel label="Notifications" value="notifications">…</ds-tab-panel>
  <ds-tab-panel label="Billing" value="billing">…</ds-tab-panel>
</ds-tabs>
```

### API

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | parameter `accessibleName` | string | Accessible name for the set of tabs. It is not shown; a visible heading above the tabs usually says the same thing. |
| `value` | attribute | parameter `value` | string | The value of the selected section. Empty or unmatched selects the first section. |
| `value` | property | parameter `value` | string | The value of the selected section. Empty or unmatched selects the first section. |
| `change` | event | event `change` |  | The selected tab changed from user interaction. |

### Section element: `<ds-tab-panel>`

| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | attribute | section parameter `label` | string | Visible text of the section's tab, and its accessible name. Required. |
| `value` | attribute | section parameter `value` | string | Identifies the section. Unique within the set; the value parameter selects the section whose value it matches. |

### Sections

Each section is a direct `ds-tab-panel` child. Its `label` attribute is the visible text of its tab,
and its `value` attribute identifies it, defaulting to the label. Values must be unique within the
tab set. Tabs follow the order of the children, and children can be added, removed, or relabeled
after connection. Other children are not rendered.

The tab set's `label` attribute names the tab list inside it, not the host, so use `label`, not
`aria-label`. Button is the one component that takes `aria-label`; the
[Button implementation](button.md) says why.

`defineTabs()` registers both elements. Pass a second tag name to alias the section element as well
as the tab set.

### Value

The `value` attribute names the selected section. Selecting a tab sets the attribute and then
dispatches `change` from the tab set. Read the `value` property for the selected section's value;
when the attribute matches no section, it returns the first section's value.

### Hidden sections

Only the selected section is assigned to the panel, so the others are not rendered and are not in
the accessibility tree. Content in hidden sections stays in the document, so form fields inside them
keep their values and still submit with their form.

content:
# Badge

Use Badge for status or metadata. It is not a control.

Labels status or metadata. Not a control.

## When to use

- Display status, category, or supporting metadata.

## When not to use

- Trigger an action in the current view. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
- Navigate to another location. Use [Link](component.link) instead. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.
- Announce a live status change by itself. Use [Alert](component.alert) instead. Badge sets no live-region role. Alert announces its message when asked to.
- Explain a status in a sentence or offer an action that resolves it. Use [Alert](component.alert) instead. Badge is a short label. Alert holds a message and actions.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| surface | indicator | Non-interactive label surface. |
| content | label | Short status or metadata text, with an optional leading icon. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | enum | `default`, `accent`, `success`, `danger`, `warning`, `info` | `default` |  |

`variant` values:

- `default`: Neutral metadata or categorization. Example: Default
- `accent`: Brand emphasis without implying status. Example: Accent
- `success`: Successful or active state. Example: Active
- `danger`: Failed or blocked status, not a destructive action. Example: Failed
- `warning`: Condition that needs attention. Example: Pending
- `info`: Informational state or feature label. Example: Beta

## States

`default`

## Rules

Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.

### Content

- **SHOULD** keep-label-short: Keep the label short.

### Behavior

- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.

### Accessibility

- **MUST** not-color-alone: The text communicates the state, so meaning does not depend on the tone's color.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone
- **MUST** no-live-region: Badge does not set a live-region role. The surrounding UI announces a status change that must be announced.
- **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, the badge keeps a visible boundary. Its tones look alike there, so its text tells them apart.
  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.

## Accessibility

- Role: Non-interactive text
- Name: Visible text is the accessible name.

## Rationale

- **Badge consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. No component-token namespace.
- **The gap between a leading icon and the label uses a spacing primitive.** Tokens ADR 0003 allows a primitive when no semantic role exists, as for padding. Badge is denser than Button, so it uses the smaller step.
- **Badge is non-interactive and sets no live-region role.** Status that must be announced belongs to the surrounding UI.

## Links

### alternative

- [Alert](component.alert) — Announce a live status change by itself. Badge sets no live-region role. Alert announces its message when asked to.
- [Alert](component.alert) — Explain a status in a sentence or offer an action that resolves it. Badge is a short label. Alert holds a message and actions.
- [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action in the current view. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
- [Link](component.link) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.

### alternative-to

- [Alert](component.alert) — Label a status or category on an item in a list or table. Badge is a compact label on an item. Alert is a message in the flow of the page.
- [Avatar](component.avatar) — Show whether a person is online, busy, or away. Avatar has no presence state in this version. Place a Badge, or text, beside it that states the status.
- [Button](component.button) — Display status or metadata. Button communicates an available action.
- [Card](component.card) — Label a status or category on an item. Badge is a compact label. Place a Badge inside a card when the card's subject has a status.
- [Link](component.link) — Display status or metadata. Link communicates a destination.

### composes

- [Icon](component.icon)

### follows

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)

### related

- [Alert](component.alert)
- [Card](component.card)
- [Text field](component.text-field)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

## Web implementation

- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
- Element: `<ds-badge>`

### Import

```js
import { defineBadge } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/badge";

defineBadge();
```

### Usage

```html
<ds-badge variant="success">Active</ds-badge>
```

# Link Use Link to navigate to another page, a location on the page, or a resource. Navigates to another page, a location on the current page, or a resource. ## When to use - Navigate to another page or resource. - Move to a location on the current page. - Point to related content from within a sentence. ## When not to use - Trigger an action or submit a form. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Buttons provide action semantics and form behavior. - Display status or metadata. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Link communicates a destination. - Switch between a few views of the same subject without leaving the page. Use [Tabs](component.tabs) instead. Tabs show one view in place. A link changes the address. ## Anatomy | Part | Role | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | control | interactive-surface | Owns the destination and focus. | | content | label | Link text with an optional decorative icon. | ## Parameters | Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | href | string | | | Destination. Without it the control is not a link and cannot receive focus. | | variant | enum | `inline`, `standalone` | `inline` | | `variant` values: - `inline`: Link inside a run of text. Inherits the surrounding typography and is always underlined. Example: token tier ADR Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#inline) - `standalone`: Link on its own line or after related content. Uses label typography and is underlined on hover. Example: View all projects Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#standalone) ## Events - `activate`: Follows the link to its destination. ## States `hover`, `focus`, `default` ## Rules Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown. ### Content - **MUST** text-describes-destination: Use link text that names the destination, not the gesture. - Do: View billing history; token tier ADR - Avoid: Click here; Learn more - **SHOULD** choose-link-or-button: Apply the action hierarchy pattern to choose between Link and Button. - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#choose-button-or-link ### Behavior - **MUST** platform-navigation: Activation navigates the way the platform's own links do, including every way the platform offers to open a destination elsewhere, such as a new tab or window. - **MUST** inline-underline: An inline link is underlined at rest, so it is distinguishable from surrounding text without color. - **SHOULD** standalone-underline-on-hover: A standalone link is underlined on hover. - **MUST** no-disabled-state: Link has no disabled state. When the destination is unavailable, render text instead of a link. - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate. - Applies when: The component is not interactive. ### Accessibility - **MUST** link-purpose: The purpose of the link is clear from its text, or from its text and the sentence around it. - **MUST** not-color-alone: An inline link does not depend on color alone to be identified. - Extends: guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state. - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus. - **MUST** guideline.accessibility#forced-colors: Under forced colors, every boundary, indicator, and focus ring that carries meaning stays visible, and each state stays distinguishable without the theme's colors. ## Accessibility - Role: Link - Name: Required from the link text. | Key | Action | | --- | --- | | Tab | Move focus to or from the link. | | Enter | Follow the link. | ## Rationale - **Link consumes semantic tokens directly.** Tokens ADR 0003. Brand foreground is audited as text on the page background, and focus already has a semantic role. No component-token namespace. - **Placement is a variant, not a size.** Inline and standalone links differ in typography and underline. Destination semantics are the same. - **The underline is not a visual mapping.** Text decoration is fixed component behavior, not a token channel. The behavior rules state when it shows. - **Link has no visited or disabled styling.** Platforms often limit visited styling to color, and no semantic visited role exists. A link with no destination is text. ## Links ### alternative - [Badge](component.badge) — Display status or metadata. Link communicates a destination. - [Button](component.button) — Trigger an action or submit a form. Buttons provide action semantics and form behavior. - [Tabs](component.tabs) — Switch between a few views of the same subject without leaving the page. Tabs show one view in place. A link changes the address. ### alternative-to - [Accordion](component.accordion) — Move between separate pages or build site navigation. Navigation belongs to links, so the address, history, and back button work. - [Badge](component.badge) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share. - [Button](component.button) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share. - [Icon](component.icon) — Navigate with an icon alone. Links provide navigation semantics and focus. - [Tabs](component.tabs) — Move between separate pages, where each choice changes the address. Navigation between pages belongs to links, so the address, history, and back button work. ### composes - [Icon](component.icon) ### follows - [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility) - [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#choose-button-or-link) - `parameters.variant.inline` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#inline) - `parameters.variant.standalone` → [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#standalone) ### related - [Tabs](component.tabs) ### used-in - [Card](component.card) ## Web implementation - Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components` - Element: `` ### Import ```js import { defineLink } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/link"; defineLink(); ``` ### Usage ```html

Themes resolve through the token tier ADR.

View all projects ``` ### API | Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `href` | attribute | parameter `href` | string | Destination. Without it the control is not a link and cannot receive focus. | | `variant` | attribute | parameter `variant` | `inline`, `standalone` | | | `click` | event | event `activate` | | Follows the link to its destination. | ### Navigation `ds-link` renders a native anchor, so activation, middle-click, modifier-click, and the browser's context menu open the destination as any link does. The browser limits `:visited` styling to color, so Link publishes no visited style. Tokens: 14 bindings, left out here.
